definitions.explanation: A question word used before a noun to ask which specific item. Always followed by a noun.

examples.japanese: どの{本|ほん}が{欲|ほ}しいですか？
どの{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}りますか？
どの{人|ひと}が{田中|たなか}さんですか？{名前|なまえ}を{聞|き}いただけなので{顔|かお}が{分|わ}かりません。
examples.english: Which person is Mr. Tanaka? I only heard his name, so I don't know his face.

examples.japanese: どの{色|いろ}が{好|す}きですか？{私|わたし}は{青|あお}が{好|す}きですが、{赤|あか}もいいと{思|おも}います。
examples.english: Which color do you like? I like blue, but I think red is nice too.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めての{場所|ばしょ}だったので、どの{道|みち}を{行|い}けばいいか{分|わ}からなくて、{駅|えき}で{人|ひと}に{聞|き}きました。
examples.english: It was my first time there, so I didn't know which road to take and asked someone at the station.

notes:
どの is a pre-noun adjectival meaning "which," always followed by a noun.

こそあど SERIES:
- この: this ~ (near speaker)
- その: that ~ (near listener)
- あの: that ~ (far from both)
- どの: which ~ (question)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- どの{人|ひと}: which person
- どの{本|ほん}: which book
- どの{電車|でんしゃ}: which train
- どのくらい/どのぐらい: how much, how long

DISTINCTION:
- どの + noun: which ~ (modifies noun)
- どれ: which one (stands alone as pronoun)

EXAMPLE CONTRAST:
どの{本|ほん}が{欲|ほ}しい？(Which book do you want?)
どれが{欲|ほ}しい？(Which one do you want?)
